title: The map
kind: a build chapter: the map that every game opens from
one: You build the map of the Mournes, with a card and a flag for each of the 8 summits. The player climbs the summits in any order, sees a tick on each one, and can finish or leave.

prev.title: Scores, the Welcome window and the Top 10

screens.title: Look at the map, from the first click to the finish

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what the map shows and what each part of it does.
**Start the expedition** on the Welcome window opens the map. The map is the middle of Summit Ready: every game opens from it, and every game comes back to it.

screenshot.alt: The map window, with the Mournes map on the left and 8 summit cards down the right
screenshot.cap: The map at the start of an expedition. No summit is climbed yet.

blocks.p: The map of the Mournes fills the left side. A small flag sits on each of the 8 summits.
Down the right side is a card for each summit. Each card shows a photo, the summit's name, its height and its game.
The player clicks a card or a flag to climb that summit. The summit's game opens, and the map hides.
The player climbs the summits in any order. When a game ends, the map comes back. That summit's flag turns into a tick, and its card turns green with the points scored.
The dark strip along the top shows the points so far, out of 800 points. It also has the speaker picture and **Back to the welcome screen**.
**Finish the expedition** ends the climb early. If summits are left, a message asks first, because those summits score 0 points.
In this chapter, no game opens yet. Chapter 9 builds a practice game, and each game chapter adds one more game to the map.

screens.title: Check that your project is ready, and see the words this chapter uses

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know that your project has everything the map needs.
The map uses things you made in earlier chapters. Check that each one is in your project before you start.

need: Your project, with the Log in window that opens the Welcome window (chapter 6).
The Expedition class, with `CurrentPlayer` in it (chapter 6).
The Welcome window, with the gold **Start the expedition** button and the Game menu (chapter 7).
The Files class, the Sound class and the Data, Images and Sounds folders in bin\Debug (chapter 2).
About 2 hours. Your ticks are kept, so you can stop at the end of any screen and come back later.

words: Cursor
The pointer the mouse shows over a control. `Cursors.Hand` is the pointing hand.
Point
A place on a window or a panel: how far across, X, and how far down, Y.
place number
The number of a summit on the map, from 0 to 7. Slieve Binnian is place 0, and Slieve Donard is place 7.
static
A field or method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. Every window reads the same `Expedition.Done`, with no object made first.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `Done[0]` is the first summit, and `Done[7]` is the 8th summit.
null
Nothing at all. A variable that holds `null` does not hold an object yet.
connect with +=
`+=` connects a method to an event in code. `card.Click += Summit_Click;` means that a click on that card runs `Summit_Click`.
Controls.Add
Puts a control that code made onto a window. Until then, the control exists, but nobody can see it.
Tag
A spare property that every control has. The map keeps each card's place number in its Tag.
Bitmap
A picture held in memory. `new Bitmap(photo, new Size(72, 48))` makes a small copy of a photo.
Environment.NewLine
Starts a new line inside some text, like pressing Enter.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(Control)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a control.
sender
Every event method is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to.
and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
switch
Picks one `case` to run, using the value in the brackets. `switch (i)` runs the case whose number matches `i`.
ShowDialog
Opens a window and waits. The code after `ShowDialog()` runs only when that window closes.
Cancel
`e.Cancel = true` stops a window from closing. It goes in FormClosing, the code that runs as a window starts to close.
blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

screens.title: Type the summits, the heights and the games into Expedition

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, the Expedition class knows the 8 summits, and what is climbed so far.
Every window needs the same 8 summits, so they live in Expedition, the class you started in chapter 6. Each list is an [[array|4]], numbered from 0 in [[place number|2]] order.

code.title: Expedition.cs: the summits and the climb so far
partLines: The class from chapter 6
You typed `CurrentPlayer` in chapter 6. The comment above the class says what the class is for.
The 8 summits
`Summits` holds the 8 names, in place order. `Summits[0]` is Slieve Binnian.
The heights
`Heights` holds each summit's height in metres, in the same order.
The games
`Games` holds the name of each summit's game, in the same order.
What is climbed so far
`Done[i]` turns true when summit `i` is climbed. `Results[i]` keeps that summit's GameResult. `new bool[8]` starts all 8 values at false.

screens.title: Make each summit card with code

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, frmMap can make one summit card and put it on the window.
8 cards are all the same apart from their words and photo, so a method makes them. Each card is a Button, made with `new Button()`, then put on the window with [[Controls.Add|7]].
Each card is 58 pixels tall, and the cards start 62 pixels apart. So card `i` starts at 64 + `i` * 62 pixels down.

code.title: MakeCard
code.why: The 8 lines in the middle set how the card looks. You set the same things in the Properties window before, so the copy already has them.
partLines: A new Button
MakeCard makes a new Button called `card`, puts it at its place down the right side and sets its size.
How the card looks
These lines set properties, as a table row does. They set a flat style, a grey border, a white background, the font, the photo on the left and the hand pointer.
The photo
The photo is loaded, and a small 72 by 48 pixel [[Bitmap|9]] copy of it goes on the card. If the photo is missing, the card has no picture, and the game carries on.
The Tag and the click
The card's [[Tag|8]] keeps its place number. `+=` connects the card's Click to Summit_Click.
Keep it and show it
`cards[i]` keeps the card, so ShowProgress can change it. `this.Controls.Add(card)` puts the card on the window.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, frmMap can make one flag and put it on its summit.
A flag is a small PictureBox. Its Parent is picMap, so the flag sits on top of the map picture. Its BackColor is transparent, so the map shows around the flag.
The flag is 32 pixels square. Taking 16 pixels off `flagX[i]` and `flagY[i]` puts the middle of the flag on the summit.

code.why: The other lines make a control in the same way as MakeCard, which you typed on the last screen.

On top of the map
A transparent background shows the map through the flag. `flag.Parent = picMap` puts the flag on the map picture, and Location puts it on the summit.
The pointer, the Tag and the click
The same as a card: the hand pointer, the place number in the Tag, and a click that runs Summit_Click.

screens.title: Open a summit's game when its card or flag is clicked

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, a click on a card or a flag runs OpenGame with that summit's place number.
Every card and every flag runs the same method, Summit_Click. `sender` is the control that was clicked, and its Tag says which summit it is.

screens.title: Any order, or one after another

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know why the map lets the player climb in any order. You will also see a simpler way for your own game.
Summit Ready lets the player choose. Each game is a different skill, so a player can start with the one they like best.
Any order needs 3 things: a Done array to remember each summit, a tick on each one, and a Finish button.
The simpler way is one after another. A single **Next summit** button opens the next place, in order. It needs no cards and no flags to click.

code.title: The other way: one summit after another
partLines: The next place
`nextPlace` starts at 0, so the first summit opens first.
Next summit
The button opens the game at `nextPlace`. If the player finished it, `nextPlace` moves on by 1.

box.title: Which way suits your own game

blocks.p: Choose one after another if each level builds on the one before, such as easy, then medium, then hard.
Choose any order if each level stands on its own, as the 8 games in Summit Ready do.

screens.title: Your turn: put your own picture and places on the map

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, the map shows your own picture, with a flag on each of your own 8 places.
Summit Ready's map is the Mourne Mountains, with a flag on each of 8 summits. Your map can be any picture with 8 places to click, such as a stage with 8 spots on it for a dance game.

Your game keeps all 8 places, so you can build more than 4 games if you have time. Each game you build fills one place. For now, a place with no game does nothing when it is clicked. Chapter 10 makes those places look tidy.

Find a square picture for your map. Make it 600 pixels wide and 600 high, so it fills picMap exactly. Open it in Paint and click **Resize**. Click **Pixels**, untick **Maintain aspect ratio**, type 600 in both boxes, then click **OK**.
Save it in the Map folder inside bin\Debug\Images, with a name such as `map-stage.png`.
Find 8 small photos, one for each place. Save them in the Summits folder inside bin\Debug\Images.

glossary: Cursor
The pointer the mouse shows over a control. `Cursors.Hand` is the pointing hand.
Point
A place on a window or a panel: how far across, X, and how far down, Y.
place number
The number of a summit on the map, from 0 to 7. Slieve Binnian is place 0, and Slieve Donard is place 7.
static
A field or method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. Every window reads the same `Expedition.Done`, with no object made first.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `Done[0]` is the first summit, and `Done[7]` is the 8th summit.
null
Nothing at all. A variable that holds `null` does not hold an object yet.
connect with +=
`+=` connects a method to an event in code. `card.Click += Summit_Click;` means that a click on that card runs `Summit_Click`.
Controls.Add
Puts a control that code made onto a window. Until then, the control exists, but nobody can see it.
Tag
A spare property that every control has. The map keeps each card's place number in its Tag.
Bitmap
A picture held in memory. `new Bitmap(photo, new Size(72, 48))` makes a small copy of a photo.
Environment.NewLine
Starts a new line inside some text, like pressing Enter.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(Control)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a control.
sender
Every event method is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to.
and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
switch
Picks one `case` to run, using the value in the brackets. `switch (i)` runs the case whose number matches `i`.
ShowDialog
Opens a window and waits. The code after `ShowDialog()` runs only when that window closes.
Cancel
`e.Cancel = true` stops a window from closing. It goes in FormClosing, the code that runs as a window starts to close.
